inputs.question: What is my ideal notice period if I am working in the private sector?
outputs.answer: The UAE Labour Law does not define an "ideal" notice period. The notice period depends on the type of employment contract and is defined by law [S1]. For employees in the private sector, the notice period is typically 30 days, unless otherwise specified in the employment contract or by law [S1]. These periods are set by law and cannot be negotiated to be shorter or longer unless otherwise agreed in writing and in compliance with the law [S1].

inputs.question: Tell me about leave.
outputs.answer: Under UAE Labour Law, workers are entitled to annual leave with full pay. For full-time workers, this is 30 days per year of service, or 2 days per month if service is more than six months but less than one year [S1]. Part-time workers receive leave based on actual working hours, with a minimum of five working days per year, calculated by converting part-time hours to full-time equivalents [S3]. Employers may allow carry-forward of up to half the annual leave to the next year or offer a cash equivalent, subject to agreement and regulations [S4]. Workers must take leave in the year it is due, unless approved for carry-forward, and employers must notify workers at least one month in advance [S1].

inputs.question: My employer has not paid my salary for two months. What does the law say?
outputs.answer: If your employer has not paid your salary for two months, the law requires that wages be paid on due dates and in accordance with the contract and Ministry regulations [S1]. All registered establishments must pay wages through the Wage Protection System or an approved system [S1]. The Ministry may take legal action against the employer for non-payment [S1]. You have the right to file a complaint with the Ministry, which can enforce payment and impose penalties [S1].

inputs.question: What did the 2022 amendment change in the Labour Law?
outputs.answer: The 2022 amendment changed clause (3) of Article (8) of the Labour Law to state that the employment contract shall be concluded for a definite period, renewable, based upon the parties' agreement [S1]. This amendment replaced the previous text of that clause [S1]. The amendment is part of Federal Decree-Law No. 14 of 2022, which amends certain provisions of Federal Decree-Law No. 33 of 2021 [S3]. Any conflicting provisions in prior laws are repealed by this amendment [S2].

inputs.question: Can my company send my personal data to another country?
outputs.answer:
Your company can send your personal data to another country only if one of the conditions in UAE PDPL Article 22 or Article 23 is met [S2][S1]. 

Under Article 22, transfer is allowed if the receiving country has data protection laws, or if there is a bilateral or multilateral agreement on data protection [S2]. 

If the receiving country does not have adequate data protection laws, transfer may still occur under Article 23 if, for example, you gave explicit consent, the transfer is necessary for a contract, or it serves public interest [S1]. 

The transfer must not contradict public or security interests [S1]. 

Your company must ensure compliance with these conditions when transferring your personal data abroad [S1][S2].
outputs.sources: ['UAE PDPL (Federal Decree-Law No. 45 of 2021), Article 23', 'UAE PDPL (Federal Decree-Law No. 45 of 2021), Article 22']

inputs.question: Do I have to pay court fees to file a labour lawsuit?
outputs.answer: No, you do not have to pay court fees to file a labour lawsuit in the UAE [S1]. Labour lawsuits are exempt from judicial fees at all stages of litigation and execution [S1]. This exemption also applies to requests submitted by workers or their heirs, as long as the value does not exceed 100,000 AED [S1].
outputs.sources: ['UAE Labour Law (Federal Decree-Law No. 33 of 2021), Article 55']

inputs.question: What does Article 51 say?
outputs.answer:
Article 51 of the UAE Labour Law (Federal Decree-Law No. 33 of 2021) outlines the end-of-service gratuity for full-time workers. 
Foreign full-time workers who have completed one or more years of continuous service are entitled to an end-of-service gratuity calculated based on their basic wage: 21 days' wage for each year of the first five years, and 30 days' wage for each year beyond that [S3]. 
The gratuity is calculated using the last basic wage received, or the average daily wage for piece-rate workers, and includes a proportional bonus for parts of a year worked [S3]. 
Days of absence without pay are not included in the service duration [S3]. 
The total gratuity must not exceed two years' wage [S3]. 
Employers may deduct lawful or court-ordered amounts from the gratuity, as per the Executive Regulation [S4]. 
The Cabinet may approve alternative gratuity systems, with conditions and contribution mechanisms specified in the decision [S4].

inputs.question: How much notice must be given to end an employment contract?
outputs.answer: The notice period, known as the warning period, must be between thirty (30) days and ninety (90) days, as specified in the employment contract [S1]. The warning period must be observed by both parties when terminating the contract, and failure to do so requires payment of a warning allowance equal to the worker's wage for the entire or remaining period [S1].

inputs.question: What is the maximum probation period?

inputs.question: How many sick leave days am I entitled to, and are they paid?
outputs.answer:

inputs.question: Tell me about leave.
outputs.answer: Workers in the UAE are entitled to annual leave with full pay, as per Article 29 of the UAE Labour Law (Federal Decree-Law No. 33 of 2021) [S2]. Full-time workers get at least 30 days of annual leave per year of service, or 2 days per month if service is more than six months but less than one year [S2]. Part-time workers are entitled to annual leave based on their actual working hours, calculated proportionally, with a minimum of five working days per year [S1][S2]. The leave must be taken in the year it is due, and the employer must notify the worker at least one month in advance [S2]. Workers may carry forward up to half of their annual leave to the next year or receive a cash equivalent, and upon termination, they are entitled to cash for unused leave based on their basic salary [S3]. Additional leaves include study leave, national service leave, mourning leave, and parental leave, which can be combined with other leaves [S4].

inputs.question: Can my company send my personal data to another country?
outputs.answer:
Your company can send your personal data to another country only if one of the conditions in UAE PDPL Article 22 or Article 23 is met [S2][S1]. 

Under Article 22, transfer is allowed if the receiving country has adequate data protection laws and a regulatory authority, or if there is a bilateral or multilateral agreement on data protection [S2]. 

If the receiving country does not have adequate protection, transfer may still occur under Article 23 if, for example, you gave explicit consent, the transfer is necessary for a contract, or it serves public interest or legal obligations [S1]. 

The transfer must not contradict public or security interests of the UAE [S1]. 

Your company must ensure compliance with these conditions before transferring your data abroad [S1][S2].

inputs.question: What does Article 51 say?
outputs.answer:
Article 51 of the UAE Labour Law (Federal Decree-Law No. 33 of 2021) states the following:

1. National workers are entitled to an end-of-service gratuity upon the end of their service, in accordance with pension and social security legislation in force [S3].
2. Foreign full-time workers who have completed one or more years of continuous service are entitled to an end-of-service gratuity calculated based on their basic wage: 21 days' wage for each year of the first five years, and 30 days' wage for each year beyond that [S3].
3. Foreign workers are entitled to a pro-rata bonus for parts of a year worked, provided they have completed at least one year of continuous service [S3].
4. Days of absence without pay are not included in the calculation of service duration [S3].
5. The gratuity is calculated based on the last basic wage for monthly, weekly, or daily wage earners, or the average daily wage for piece-rate workers [S3].
6. The total end-of-service gratuity for a foreign worker must not exceed two years' wage [S3].
7. Employers may deduct amounts due by law or by judgment from the gratuity, under conditions and procedures specified by the Executive Regulation [S4].
8. The Cabinet may approve alternative end-of-service gratuity systems upon the Minister’s proposal and coordination with concerned authorities, specifying conditions, controls, and contribution mechanisms [S4].

inputs.question: How much notice must be given to end an employment contract?
outputs.answer: The notice period, known as the warning period, must be between thirty (30) days and ninety (90) days, as specified in the employment contract [S1]. This period must be adhered to by both parties when terminating the contract, unless otherwise agreed upon in the interest of the worker [S1]. If the warning period is not observed, the non-complying party must pay a warning allowance equal to the worker’s wage for the full or remaining warning period [S1]. The warning period does not start during the worker’s leave unless both parties agree otherwise [S2].

inputs.question: How many sick leave days am I entitled to, and are they paid?
outputs.answer:
After the probation period, you are entitled to a maximum of 90 sick leave days per year, calculated as follows: 
- First 15 days: full pay [S1]. 
- Next 30 days: half pay [S1]. 
- Remaining 45 days: unpaid [S1].

inputs.question: How many days of annual leave do I get?
outputs.answer:
You are entitled to annual leave based on your service period:

- If you have completed one year or more of continuous service, you are entitled to 30 days of annual leave with full pay [S1].
- If your service period is more than six months but less than one year, you are entitled to two days of annual leave for each month worked [S1].
- If your employment ends before you use your annual leave balance, you are entitled to a leave for the portion of the year you worked [S1].
- For part-time workers, the annual leave is calculated based on actual working hours, with a minimum of five working days per year [S2].

The exact number depends on your total service duration and working hours.

inputs.question: Tell me about leave.
outputs.answer:
Workers in the UAE are entitled to annual leave with full pay under the UAE Labour Law (Federal Decree-Law No. 33 of 2021), Article 29 [S1][S2]. 

- Full-time workers get 30 days of annual leave per year of service, or 2 days per month if service is between six months and one year [S1]. 
- Part-time workers are entitled to annual leave based on actual working hours, with a minimum of five working days per year, calculated by converting part-time hours to full-time equivalents [S3]. 
- Annual leave must be taken in the year it is earned, but may be carried forward with employer approval [S2]. 
- Employers must notify workers of leave dates at least one month in advance [S1]. 
- Workers are also entitled to paid leave for mourning (5 days for spouse, 3 days for other relatives), parental leave (5 working days within 6 months of birth), and study leave (10 business days per year for those with at least 2 years of service) [S4]. 
- The Executive Regulation specifies further rules for organizing and compensating leave [S1][S2][S4].

outputs.answer: The 2022 Amendment changed clause (3) of Article (8) of the UAE Labour Law, replacing it to state that the employment contract shall be concluded for a definite period, renewable, based upon the parties' agreement [S1]. The amendment came into force the day after its publication in the Official Gazette [S3].

inputs.question: Can my company send my personal data to another country?
outputs.answer:
Your company can send your personal data to another country only if one of the conditions in UAE PDPL Article 22 or Article 23 is met [S2][S1]. 

Under Article 22, transfer is allowed if the receiving country has data protection laws, or if there is a bilateral/multilateral agreement on data protection [S2]. 

Under Article 23, transfer is allowed if you gave explicit consent, the transfer is necessary for legal obligations, contract implementation, judicial cooperation, or public interest, and it does not harm national security [S1]. 

The transfer must also comply with any requirements set by the UAE Data Protection Bureau [S2]. 

Your company must ensure that appropriate safeguards are in place, such as contracts or judicial orders, especially if the receiving country lacks strong data protection laws [S1].

inputs.question: Do I have to pay court fees to file a labour lawsuit?
outputs.answer: No, you do not have to pay court fees to file a labour lawsuit in the UAE [S1]. Labour lawsuits are exempt from judicial fees at all stages of litigation and execution [S1]. This exemption also applies to requests submitted by workers or their heirs, as long as the value does not exceed 100,000 AED [S1].

inputs.question: What does Article 51 say?
outputs.answer:
Article 51 of the UAE Labour Law (Federal Decree-Law No. 33 of 2021) states the following:

1. National workers are entitled to an end-of-service gratuity upon the end of their service, in accordance with pension and social security legislation in force [S3].
2. Foreign full-time workers who have completed one or more years of continuous service are entitled to an end-of-service gratuity calculated based on their basic wage: 21 days' wage for each year of the first five years, and 30 days' wage for each year beyond that [S3].
3. Foreign workers are entitled to a pro-rata bonus for parts of a year worked, provided they have completed at least one year of continuous service [S3].
4. Days of absence without pay are not included in the calculation of service duration [S3].
5. The gratuity is calculated based on the last basic wage for monthly, weekly, or daily wage earners, or the average daily wage for piece-rate workers [S3].
6. The total end-of-service gratuity for a foreign worker must not exceed two years' wage [S3].
7. Employers may deduct amounts due by law or by judgment from the gratuity, under conditions and procedures specified by the Executive Regulation [S4].
8. The Cabinet may approve alternative end-of-service gratuity systems upon the Minister’s proposal and coordination with concerned authorities, specifying conditions, controls, and contribution mechanisms [S4].

If the warning period is not followed, the non-complying party must pay a warning allowance equal to the worker’s wage for the entire or remaining warning period [S1]. The warning period does not start during the worker’s leave, unless both parties agree otherwise [S2].

to in this article, if he is unable to return to work, provided that the Worker receives all his

Regulation.", "[Labour Law — Article 32]

a. A mourning leave of five (5) days, in the event of the death of the spouse; and Three
(3) days in the event of the death of the mother, father, son, brother, sister, grandson,
grandfather or grandmother, starting as of the date of death.

or the mother) who has a child, to care for his child, to be enjoyed, continuously or
intermittently, within a period of six (6) months as of the date of the child's birth.
c. Any other leaves determined by the Cabinet.

for the Worker who is enrolled - by affiliation or regularly - in one of the educational
institutions approved in the State, in order to perform the tests, provided th at the period
of service with the Employer is not less than two years.

service with pay, in accordance with the legislation in force in the State.

following:
a. The first forty-five (45) days with full pay.
b. The following fifteen (15) days with half pay.

a period not exceeding forty-five (45) consecutive or intermittent days, if such absence is
due to an illness suffered by her or her child as a result of pregnancy or childbirth and that
does not enable her to return to her work. Said illness shall be proven by a medical
certificate issued by the Medical Authority, and this period shall not be included in the
period of service for which the female Worker is entitled to the end of service gratui ty or
the period of contribution to the retirement system in accordance with the legislation in
force in this regard.

determined by a Cabinet resolution.

the basic wage for that day.']

inputs.question: How many days of annual leave do I get?
outputs.answer:
You are entitled to annual leave based on your service period:

- If you have completed one year or more of service, you are entitled to 30 days of annual leave with full pay [S1].
- If your service period is more than six months but less than one year, you are entitled to 2 days of annual leave per month [S1].
- If your employment ends before using your annual leave balance, you are entitled to leave for the portion of the year you worked [S1].
- Part-time workers are entitled to annual leave based on their actual working hours, with a minimum of 5 working days per year [S2].

The exact number depends on your total service duration and working hours.
